def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain relative path that stays inside the
    directory it is resolved against. Empty names, absolute paths, names
    with a ".." component, backslashes or NUL characters are not safe."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("sub/a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/../../b") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if name.char_count() == 0:
        return False
    if name.startswith("/"):
        return False
    if "\\" in name:
        return False
    if "\0" in name:
        return False
    for part in name.split("/"):
        if part == "..":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read from the directory
    notes, or "" when none can. Reading happens inside
    `with fs = fs.sub("notes"):`, so fs is confined to notes. A name that
    fails is_safe_name, or that is missing or unreadable, is skipped.
    Returns "" for an empty list."""
    result = ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not is_safe_name(name):
                continue
            text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
            if text != "":
                result = text
                break
    return result
